# zero-qs

The query string parser with pair, depth, and array caps for zero-server.

[API reference](https://molexxxx.github.io/zero-server/docs/reference/rust/zero_qs/index.html) | [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/zero-qs) | [docs.rs](https://docs.rs/zero-qs)

## The same capability in every language

| Language | Package | Reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rust | [`zero-router`](https://crates.io/crates/zero-router) | [reference](https://molexxxx.github.io/zero-server/docs/reference/rust/zero_router/index.html), [docs.rs](https://docs.rs/zero-router), [install](https://molexxxx.github.io/zero-server/docs/reference/rust.html#rust-router) |
| Rust | [`zero-uri`](https://crates.io/crates/zero-uri) | [reference](https://molexxxx.github.io/zero-server/docs/reference/rust/zero_uri/index.html), [docs.rs](https://docs.rs/zero-uri), [install](https://molexxxx.github.io/zero-server/docs/reference/rust.html#rust-router) |
| Rust | [`zero-qs`](https://crates.io/crates/zero-qs) | [reference](https://molexxxx.github.io/zero-server/docs/reference/rust/zero_qs/index.html), [docs.rs](https://docs.rs/zero-qs), [install](https://molexxxx.github.io/zero-server/docs/reference/rust.html#rust-router) |

The TypeScript, Python and C# packages of this capability ship in a later release.

The query string parser of zero-server: `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`
as the URL Standard defines it, for query components and form bodies.

The parser splits the input on `&`, skips empty sequences, splits each
sequence at its first `=` (a sequence without one is a name with an empty
value), turns `+` into a space in names and values, percent-decodes with a `%`
that is not followed by two hexadecimal digits kept as it is, and decodes the
bytes as UTF-8 without a byte order mark, replacing invalid sequences with
U+FFFD. Pairs come out as the caller iterates, so the input bounds the work and
nothing is kept beyond the pair in hand.

## struct `Pairs`

The pairs of a query string, in order.

### `Pairs <'a>::next_pair`

The next name and value, decoded.

**Returns**

The pair, or `None` at the end of the input.

```rust
fn next_pair(&mut self) -> Option <(String, String)>
```

### `Pairs <'a>::next_raw`

The next name and value as the bytes between the delimiters, with `+` and
percent-encoding untouched.

```rust
fn next_raw(&mut self) -> Option <(&'a [u8], &'a [u8])>
```

## fn `parse`

Parse a query string or form body.

**Arguments**

* `input` - the bytes, without the leading `?` of a query component.

**Returns**

The pairs, decoded as the caller iterates.

```rust
fn parse(input: &[u8]) -> Pairs <'_>
```

## fn `parse_all`

Parse a query string into a list of pairs.

**Arguments**

* `input` - the bytes.
* `max_pairs` - the most pairs to keep; the rest of the input is left unread.

```rust
fn parse_all(input: &[u8], max_pairs: usize) -> Vec <(String, String)>
```

## fn `get`

The first value for `name`, decoded.

**Arguments**

* `input` - the query string.
* `name` - the name to look for, compared after decoding.

```rust
fn get(input: &[u8], name: &str) -> Option <String>
```

## fn `decode`

Decode one name or value: `+` to a space, percent-decoding with a bare `%`
kept, then UTF-8 without a byte order mark and with U+FFFD for invalid
sequences.

**Arguments**

* `input` - the bytes between the delimiters.

```rust
fn decode(input: &[u8]) -> String
```
